summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for recurrent acute pancreatitis and a pancreatic tail cyst. She underwent a distal pancreatectomy with splenectomy and a small intestinal full-thickness biopsy. Postoperatively, she followed a modified Whipple pathway, with NG tube removal on postoperative day 1 and gradual diet advancement. Pain was managed with PCA initially, then transitioned to oral medications. JP drain was removed on postoperative day 6 after amylase testing. She tolerated a regular diet, had bowel movements, and recovered well. Pathology showed no cyst or pancreatitis in the resected pancreas, and the small bowel biopsy was normal. She was discharged home on postoperative day 6 with instructions for wound care, activity restrictions, vaccinations due to asplenia, and follow-up with surgery and gastroenterology.
